messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> continuous-batching: high-concurrency perf cliff detected on us-west-2. 90th latency > 3s, error rate rising. Paging eng-oncall.

eva: saw this pop up ~2m ago. A lot of queueing on the cb worker pool, microbatch sizes ballooning.

mike: confirming — kvcache eviction spikes correlating with the perf cliff. looks like a cache blowout plus jitter causing huge microbatch aggregation. stack: cb-v2 with adaptive-prefetch.

lee: customer impact? any 5xxs?

sarah: yes 503/504s up for some hosted routes. sample: auth-proxy 503 spike ~10% for top customers. Not widespread but some Dedicated customers hit higher tail latency.

mike: metrics dump:  
```
kvcache.evictions.count: 12480/min
continuous_batch.microbatch.size.p95: 2300
continuous_batch.queue_depth: 420
worker.latency.90p: 3.8s
requests.5xx.rate: +9.4% (last 5m)
```

mike: microbatch target was 256 -> something in the batching logic allowed growth up to 4096 under high concurrency combined with jittered timers. Prefetch/pinning made KV entries hot then evicted due to pressure.

eva: first mitigation: throttle the ingress concurrency to limit batch growth. I'm going to flip the route-level soft-rate-limit to 70% for the busiest routes.

ops-bot: ACTION: set-route-capacity --route-id r-prod-gen --qps-limit 0.7 --apply-now (initiated by eva)

lee: also reduce continuous_batch.max_batch_tokens on the hot pool to 512 and drop the microbatch accumulation window from 200ms -> 40ms to reduce jitter coalescing.

mike: proposed hotfix commands (rolling, canary 10%):
```
# disable adaptive-prefetch quick rollback
redwood-admin rollout set-config --pool cb-usw2-hot --key continuous_batch.adaptive_prefetch --value false --canary 0.1
# cap microbatch tokens
redwood-admin rollout set-config --pool cb-usw2-hot --key continuous_batch.max_batch_tokens --value 512 --canary 0.1
```

sarah: i pushed the canary to 10% on the hot pool. observing trace. initial tail lat down ~30% on canary nodes. customers on canary show fewer 5xxs.

eva: i'm also lowering route concurrency on the edge for 5 routes with highest qps. doing a 5-min ramp down. will watch backpressure.

mike: additional temporary mitigation: increase kvcache.eviction_threshold to avoid eager evictions during the blowout. command: 
```
redwood-admin set-metric-config --pool cb-usw2-hot --key kvcache.eviction_threshold --value 0.85 --canary 0.1
```

lee: coordinating with infra — if eviction_threshold change causes memory pressure we roll back immediately. infra on standby.

incident-bot: NOTE: alert suppressed for 10m while canary stabilizes (triggered by sarah)

mike: after canary rollout to 10% and the route soft-limit, p95 dropped from 3.8s -> 2.1s on canary nodes; 5xxs decreased by ~60% on canary traffic. queue depth down to 120. still higher than steady state but manageable.

eva: plan: continue canary to 33% if metrics keep improving. do not change model variants or quantization. main goal: prevent KV thrash and reduce microbatch coalescing.

sarah: heads-up: customer success flagged two enterprise customers — outreach in progress. no data integrity issues, just degraded latency.

lee: handing off to night oncall (mike) at 4481234800. summary for handoff message:
- incident: continuous-batch perf cliff at high concurrency causing queueing and kvcache evictions
- mitigation: canary config changes (adaptive_prefetch=false, max_batch_tokens=512), route soft-rate-limit 70%, eviction_threshold raised to 0.85
- impact: elevated 5xxs for some hosted & dedicated customers, partial recovery on canary nodes
- followups: postmortem, investigate adaptive-prefetch heuristics, tighten microbatch growth limits, add automatic guardrail to cap microbatch.size under hot jackrabbit condition

mike: acked for handoff. i'll keep an eye on the canary -> 33% ramp. if p95 remains >2.5s abort ramp and roll config back.

eva: also creating a quick monitoring dashboard and a regression alarm for microbatch.size.p95 crossing 1000 for more than 30s.

ops-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff scheduled to mike at 4481234800 (created by lee)

sarah: tagging compliance: no customer data escaped, only latency/regressions.

lee: adding short-lived runbook entry in /runbooks/continuous-batch/high-concurrency.md (ops ticket created) — will include exact rollback commands and the decision criteria.

mike: current action items:
- keep canary at 10% for 10m, then 33% if stable (mike)
- contact two affected customers w/ status and ETA (sarah)
- postmortem and code-level fixes for adaptive-prefetch and batcher heuristics (eva + eng-ml)
eva: thanks everyone. if it resurges i'll page infra and escalate to platform leads.

mike: closing active pager for now but leaving thread open for handoff notes and postmortem links. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigation applied, suppression active, oncall handoff pending.
